city.Romania.description: This country in Eastern Europe is famous for the misty Transylvania mountains, a spooky hilltop castle linked to the Dracula story, and wild wetlands where the Danube River spreads out before reaching the sea.
city.Romania.landmark: pointed turrets of Bran Castle rising from a forested crag in Transylvania
city.Romania.greeting: In Romanian, hello is “Bună ziua” (BOO-nuh ZEE-wah), meaning good day.
city.Romania.flag: doodled a flag with three tall stripes of blue, yellow and red
city.Romania.clue.0: asked about flights to a country in Eastern Europe wrapped in a horseshoe of green mountains
city.Romania.clue.1: couldn't wait to visit a spooky hilltop castle famous from the Dracula story
city.Serbia.description: This landlocked country in the Balkans of southeastern Europe is known for its lively capital Belgrade, loud brass-band music festivals, old cliffside monasteries, and a winding river canyon where huge vultures nest.
city.Serbia.landmark: dramatic hairpin meanders of the Uvac River canyon seen from the clifftops
city.Serbia.flag: red, blue and white stripes with a shield topped by a double-headed eagle
city.Serbia.clue.0: circled a landlocked country in the Balkans of southeastern Europe on a map
city.Slovakia.description: This small, landlocked country in Central Europe has more castles for its size than almost anywhere, old wooden churches built without a single nail, and the rugged, forested peaks of the Carpathian Mountains.
city.Slovakia.landmark: fairy-tale white towers of Bojnice Castle above green parkland
city.Slovakia.greeting: In Slovak, a friendly hello is “Ahoj” (AH-hoy).
city.Slovakia.flag: pinned on a flag badge: white, blue and red stripes with a red shield showing a white double cross standing on three blue hills
city.Slovakia.clue.0: kept talking about a land that has more fairy-tale castles than almost anywhere on Earth
city.Slovakia.clue.1: was amazed by old wooden churches built entirely without using a single nail
city.Slovenia.description: This green country in Central Europe, near the Alps and the Adriatic Sea, is famous for storybook Lake Bled with its island church, enormous underground caves, and forests that cover more than half the land.
city.Slovenia.landmark: island church on Lake Bled with the clifftop castle and Alps behind
city.Slovenia.greeting: In Slovene, you can say hello with “Živjo” (ZHEEV-yo).
city.Slovenia.flag: white, blue and red stripes with a shield of three snowy peaks and three gold stars
city.Slovenia.clue.0: couldn't wait to explore giant underground caves full of strange dripping rock shapes
city.Slovenia.clue.1: kept asking to see the olm, a pale little salamander people call a 'baby dragon'
city.Sweden.description: This long country in Northern Europe is known for cozy design and pop music, thousands of rocky islands scattered along its coast, and a far north where the midnight sun and northern lights fill the sky.
city.Sweden.landmark: colorful waterfront townhouses of Stockholm's old town
city.Sweden.greeting: In Swedish, hello is “Hej” (hey) — nice and easy!
city.Sweden.flag: traced a flag: deep blue with a bright yellow cross reaching to the edges
city.Sweden.clue.0: hoped to spend a night in a hotel carved entirely from blocks of snow and ice
city.Switzerland.description: This mountainous country in Central Europe sits high among the snowy Alps and is famous for chocolate, cheese, fancy watches, and the sharp, pyramid-shaped peak of the Matterhorn.
